Once upon a time, a little girl lived with her mum at the edge of a big green wood.
Her grandma had made her a bright red hood, and she wore it every single day.
So everybody called her Red Riding Hood.
Her little white puppy, Button, went everywhere with her.
One morning, Mum packed a basket of honey cakes and apples for Grandma's birthday.
Stay on the path all the way, okay?
said Mum.
If a stranger asks you to leave the path, just say no, thank you, and tell a grown-up you know.
I stay on the path, all the way to Grandma's!
said Red Riding Hood.
Red Riding Hood waved bye-bye, and off she went, with the basket on her arm and Button trotting along beside her.
Tip, tap, tip, tap, went her little red boots along the path.
In the middle of the wood, a big grey Wolf was sitting on a log by the path.
He looked lost, and his tummy was rumbling.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
Hello,
said Wolf.
I'm new in this wood, and I can't find my way.
Do you want to come and pick blackberries with me, over there in the trees?
I'm so hungry, and I've got nobody to play with.
No, thank you,
Oh, okay,
said Wolf, and his ears drooped a little.
Soon she met the Woodcutter, Grandma's friend, stacking logs by the path.
A Wolf I don't know asked me to leave the path, so I said no, thank you,
Well done, you! You stayed on the path, and you told me,
said Woodcutter.
The Woodcutter put down his logs.
He took Red Riding Hood's hand, and they went back to see if the Wolf needed help.
Hello, Wolf. Are you okay?
I'm lost, and I'm hungry, and I haven't got a single friend,
His tummy rumbled again.
It's Grandma's birthday today. Come to her party with us!
She always says there's room for one more.
So they all walked along the path together, and the Wolf wagged and wagged his tail.
sang Red Riding Hood.
Knock!
Who's there?
said Grandma.
It's me, Red Riding Hood, and I've brought some friends!
Grandma opened the door wide.
Come in, come in! There's always room for one more!
Everybody sat round Grandma's little table, and they shared the honey cakes and apples from the basket.
Happy birthday, Grandma!
The Wolf munched three honey cakes.
Mmm! Yum, yum, yum!
This is the yummiest cake in the whole wood!
Grandma's spare glasses were lying on the table.
Can I try them on?
Of course you can!
The Wolf put them on, and his eyes looked big and round!
Wolf, what big eyes you have!
All the better to see you with!
Ha, ha, ha!
Hee, hee, hee!
Everybody laughed.
Next, the Wolf tried on Grandma's fluffy pink earmuffs from the peg by the door.
They were way too small for his big pointy ears!
Wolf, what big ears you have!
All the better to hear you with!
Then the Wolf smiled the biggest, happiest smile of all.
Wolf, what a big smile you have!
That's because I'm not lost any more,
I've got friends now!
And Grandma gave him a great big, warm hug.
That night, snuggled up in bed, Red Riding Hood told Mum all about her day.
I stayed on the path, and I told a grown-up,
Well done, sweetheart,
said Mum, and she kissed her goodnight.
Button was fast asleep at her feet.
From that day on, the Wolf came to Grandma's for honey cake every Sunday.
